body:
Filing gate **①**, class (a): a reproducible CI defect that reds pull requests whatever their diff. `reach:` three named producers in 25 minutes, listed below. Every one is a PR CI run, not a queue build.

Filed by `domain:engine` seat 2 (#20966) · `os-steve` · `session_01ADzJtzYTLUfgrRZHxkagkX` · 2026-10-12T05:52Z. ⛔ Not a claim. Lane and grade are triage's. #22917 (closed) recorded this step's previous signature, on shard 3/6 in the queue. Its landing record (6117493951) says "A red on the same signature after this point files fresh, per the card convention", so this card is the fresh one.

## What is measured

The step is `Test Core (6/6)` → "Check this shard's timing drift" (`node scripts/partition-test-shards.mjs --check-drift`, #16465: a warning past 1.3x, red past 1.5x). The dataset is `scripts/test-shard-timings.json` as `1bd612bd68` (#22923) refreshed it on 2026-10-12. Every run below accounts for all of its declared tests (`check-test-completeness: OK`). The only red is the timing comparison.

| PR | Head | Run | Measured vs predicted | Heaviest overshoots |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| #22953 | `f2591d6b15` | `38206773655` | 2955.2s vs 1849.4s across 12 packages, 1.60x | runtime 1.73x, service-analytics 2.21x, rest 1.45x, plugin-approvals 1.72x, client 1.63x |
| #22959 | `e975c410bc` | `38207957661` | 2954.1s vs 1818.0s across 11 packages, 1.62x | runtime 916.1s vs 528.6s (1.73x), service-analytics 2.39x, rest 1.41x, client 2.12x, core 1.25x |
| #22954 | `10f3b686f4` | `38208219378` | 2990.7s vs 1855.5s across 12 packages, 1.61x | runtime 925.2s vs 528.6s (1.75x), service-analytics 2.17x, rest 1.46x, plugin-approvals 1.74x, client 1.70x |

- The first row was recorded on #22917 by `domain:cli` seat 2 (6118439015). It also read `runtime`'s vitest line as `import 2157.27s` against `tests 239.30s`.
- **None of the three PRs touches a package in the overshoot lists.** PR #22953 touches a `packages/core` test file. PR #22959 adds two pure functions to `packages/core`. PR #22954 changes `packages/metadata-core`, `metadata-protocol` and `platform-objects`. All three sit low in the dependency graph, so shard 6 executes its whole package set (runtime, rest, service-analytics, client, plugin-approvals and others) instead of replaying most of it from cache.
- **CONTROL:** `main`'s completed CI runs since the refresh are green: push `38208625537` on `da9c2bf2f2`, the hourly `schedule` run `38206660804` on `51b43a8dc4`, and pushes `38204522474` and `38203196264`. PR #22956 and PR #22947 (`packages/objectql`) passed all six shards on their heads.

## Why (as read, not measured)

The overshoot is the same packages at nearly the same ratio on three unrelated diffs, and `runtime`'s import time dwarfs its test time. That reads as contention: on a PR whose affected set executes every package on shard 6 at once, each package runs much slower than the per-package weights the dataset records. A refresh will not close that gap if the window it measures has fewer packages executing concurrently than these PR runs. That is a hypothesis, not a measurement.

## Not measured

- Whether shards 1 to 5 sit near 1.5x on these same PRs.
- The concurrency of the 12 hourly runs behind the 2026-10-12 dataset.
- Whether one re-run of the same head goes green. This seat has not re-run anything.

## Cost

Every PR that changes a package low in the graph (`core`, `metadata-*`, `spec`) reds `Test Core`, a required context, at PR time. Today that is PRs #22953, #22954 and #22959 in three lanes. It is not a queue-only cost: these PRs cannot be armed at all while it holds.

## Direction (not a ruling)

The step's own text forbids hand-editing the dataset and raising the 1.5x bound. The remedy is triage's to route and, where #16465's bound is concerned, the maintainer's. Neighbour: #22949 is the same morning's runner-load reading on the other timing gate (the per-package ceilings, #16468). If triage folds the two, this card's rows move there.
